items.title: 8.14 The effect of a change in temperature

blocks.text: Le Chatelier's principle predicts the direction of a reaction when the temperature changes, and temperature is the only factor that also changes the value of the equilibrium constant. For an exothermic reaction an increase in temperature (adding heat) favours the reverse reaction and a decrease favours the forward reaction. For 2SO2(g) + O2(g) giving 2SO3(g), delta H = -198 kJ, raising the temperature shifts the reaction from right to left: SO3 decreases, SO2 and O2 increase, and the equilibrium constant decreases; lowering the temperature favours the forward reaction and the formation of SO3, which is favoured at low temperature. Kc for this reaction is 2.8 x 10^2 at 1000 K but 1 x 10^26 at 298 K.

For an endothermic reaction an increase in temperature favours the forward reaction and a decrease favours the reverse. For N2O4(g) giving 2NO2(g), delta H = +57.2 kJ, raising the temperature shifts the reaction from left to right: N2O4 decreases, NO2 increases and Kc increases; lowering the temperature shifts it from right to left and favours the reactant. Kc for this reaction is 7.7 x 10^-5 at 273 K and 0.4 at 373 K.
